branch.title: From Maxwell to QED: a history in a growing network

extra.description: Measured from a body's acceleration (F = ma) or by balancing it against a known force. Every force law in the story predicts it, so more and more alternative routes lead here.
Where a body sits in Euclidean 3-space, measured with rulers. Separations r = x − x′ enter every force law. A primitive geometric observable.
v = dx/dt from successive position measurements. It becomes essential once magnetic forces turn out to depend on motion.
Position and velocity together: Newton's description of a body's state.
extra.math_structure: Point of the tangent bundle Tℝ³; over time, a curve x(t).

extra.description: How forces and fields combine. Because order and grouping do not matter, the total force from any number of sources is well defined.
Generates time evolution. Its commuting with spatial derivatives is used when the curl equations are combined into wave equations.
A signed scalar property of bodies, inferred from the forces they exert on one another. Experimentally additive and conserved, and (Millikan) quantized in units of e.
Franklin's principle: charges add with sign, and electrification only moves charge from one body to another. A global statement that the continuity equation later makes local.
k q₁q₂ r̂/r² with k = 1/4πε₀. Exchange symmetry gives Newton's third law; the inverse-square form is exactly what makes Gauss's law hold.
The simplest state of an electrostatic system: which charges there are and where they sit.
extra.math_structure: A point in ℝ³ᴺ with a charge label qᵢ on each of N points.

extra.description: The map from sources to forces and fields is linear: contributions from separate sources simply add. Exact in vacuum Maxwell theory.
∇²φ = −ρ/ε₀. Linearity means solutions superpose; uniqueness means sources plus boundary data fully determine the state.
Charge per unit volume. Smooth densities and point charges (via δ functions) are elements of the same space.
extra.math_structure: Scalar distribution (signed measure) on ℝ³.

extra.description: Lets point charges and smooth densities live in one space: ρ = Σ qᵢ δ³(x − xᵢ). Introduced by Dirac (1927) and made rigorous by Schwartz (1945).
The electrostatic state written as one scalar function, with its built-in redundancy made explicit.
extra.math_structure: Element of the quotient C^∞(ℝ³)/ℝ: an equivalence class of functions differing by constants.

extra.description: The part of the state fixed by conductors and the outside world. Needed to make Poisson's problem well posed.
extra.math_structure: Values φ|∂Ω (Dirichlet) or ∂φ/∂n (Neumann) on boundary surfaces.

extra.description: Because ∇ kills constants, φ and φ + c give the same force. This is the first redundancy (gauge freedom) in the description of the state.
Converts local statements about sources into statements about flux through surfaces, and back. Also used for any flux integral.
Φ_E = ∮E·dA through a closed surface. Gauss's law says it equals Q_enc/ε₀ however the enclosed charges are arranged.
If a source distribution is unchanged by rotations, translations or reflections, the field it produces must transform the same way. With Gauss's or Ampère's law this fixes fields without integrating.
Operationally E = lim F/q for a small test charge at rest: a derived observable built from force and charge measurements.
The whole field as one object, a function on space. A calculating device for Green and Gauss; a physical state for Faraday and Maxwell.
extra.math_structure: Vector field ℝ³ → ℝ³ (curl-free in statics).

extra.description: Integrals along curves. Path independence holds for curl-free fields on regions without holes; the exception returns with holonomy in the final section.
Work needed to assemble a configuration from charges far apart. Measured through work done or heat released on discharge.
U(E₁ + E₂) = U(E₁) + U(E₂) + a cross term. The cross term is why energies do not simply add even though fields do.
Volta's tension, a potential difference φ(b) − φ(a): what a voltmeter reads. Invariant under φ → φ + const, which is why it is measurable while φ itself is not.
C = Q/ΔV for a conductor or pair of conductors. Depends only on geometry (and the medium) because electrostatics is linear.
I = dQ/dt through a surface, read by an ammeter. Equal to the flux of the current density.
Charge flux per unit area. Together with ρ it specifies all the sources of the field.
extra.math_structure: Vector field J(x, t); in steady flow ∇·J = 0.

extra.description: R = ΔV/I for a conductor. Ohm found it independent of the current for a given wire at fixed temperature.
J = σE inside a conductor, or ΔV = IR for a whole wire. Unlike Maxwell's equations it describes a material, valid for many conductors at moderate fields.
Charge cannot vanish in one place and reappear in another: change inside a volume equals flux through its boundary. Later developments derive it rather than assume it.
The magnetic action at a point, read with a compass or a probe coil, or inferred from the velocity-dependent force on a moving charge.
Field of a current element, (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r². The magnetic counterpart of the Coulomb law.
a×b = −b×a, and a×(b×c) ≠ (a×b)×c. Its dependence on handedness makes B a pseudovector, and since v×B ⟂ v, magnetic forces do no work.
Measures circulation. The identity div∘curl = 0 is what later forces the displacement current.
The magnetic field as a single object on space.
extra.math_structure: Divergence-free pseudovector field on ℝ³.

extra.description: ℰ = ∮(E + v×B)·dl around a circuit, measured as the voltage across a small gap in the loop.
Φ_B = ∫B·dA through a surface bounded by a loop: Faraday's count of lines of force threading a circuit.
A changing magnetic flux induces a circulating electric field; the minus sign makes induced currents oppose the change.
Neumann's and Thomson's potential, Maxwell's electromagnetic momentum. Useful for calculation; not observable by itself.
extra.math_structure: Vector field A(x, t) whose curl is B: one representative of a gauge class.

extra.description: Fix the strength of electric forces between charges and magnetic forces between currents. 1/√(ε₀μ₀) is the speed Weber and Kohlrausch found as a ratio of units. (In the 2019 SI they are fixed through the measured fine-structure constant.)
Measured astronomically (Rømer 1676, Bradley 1729) and on Earth by Fizeau (1849). After Maxwell it is also predicted from ε₀ and μ₀. Only the prediction is drawn as a route; the measurements are not.
The complete field law. Gauss's two laws constrain each moment; Faraday's and the Ampère–Maxwell law evolve it.
Electric and magnetic fields as one state that evolves in time.
extra.math_structure: Pair of vector fields with ∇·E = ρ/ε₀ and ∇·B = 0 at one time: Cauchy data.

extra.description: u = ½(ε₀|E|² + |B|²/μ₀). Integrates to the total energy stored in the field.
Expresses the force on charges inside a volume as a surface integral over the field around them.
□ = c⁻²∂²/∂t² − ∇². Choosing the retarded Green's function means influences travel at c from the past.
A rule that picks one pair (φ, A) from each class, chosen to simplify the equations.
(φ, A) → (φ − ∂χ/∂t, A + ∇χ). Two transformations compose in either order to χ₁ + χ₂: the group is commutative.
The physical state in the potential description. Everything observable is a function of these classes.
extra.math_structure: Orbit of the gauge group in the space of pairs (φ, A): a point of a quotient space.

extra.description: ∇·B = 0 ⇒ B = ∇×A, and ∇×(E + ∂A/∂t) = 0 ⇒ E + ∂A/∂t = −∇φ. It can fail on regions with holes, which is where holonomy lives.
∂u/∂t + ∇·S = −J·E: field energy changes by flowing away or by doing work on charges.
S = E×B/μ₀, the energy flux in W/m². Its time average is the intensity a detector measures.
Wavelength, frequency and polarization, measured with standing waves, interferometers and polarizers. In vacuum ω = c|k| and k ⟂ E ⟂ B.
The source-free field described by its modes rather than by its values at points.
extra.math_structure: Amplitudes a(k, λ) for wave vectors k and two transverse polarizations λ.

extra.description: Writes any field as a superposition of plane waves e^{i(k·x − ωt)}, in which the field equations become algebraic.
g = S/c². Observed as radiation pressure on mirrors and absorbers.
Energy per unit time leaving an accelerating charge through a distant sphere.
Two non-parallel boosts compose to a boost plus a rotation (the Wigner rotation). Under boosts, E and B mix.
Scalar and vector potentials as a single spacetime object.
extra.math_structure: 1-form A on Minkowski spacetime with components (φ/c, A).

extra.description: Charge and current density as a single spacetime object.
extra.math_structure: Vector field on spacetime (cρ, J), equivalently the 3-form ⋆J.

extra.description: Electric and magnetic fields as one observer-independent object.
extra.math_structure: Antisymmetric rank-2 tensor (2-form) on spacetime; F₀ᵢ ∝ Eᵢ/c, Fᵢⱼ ∝ εᵢⱼₖBₖ.

extra.description: E·B and |E|² − c²|B|² take the same value for every inertial observer. If E ⟂ B and |E| < c|B|, some frame sees a purely magnetic field.
One symmetric tensor whose components, for a given observer, are the energy density, Poynting flux, momentum density and Maxwell stress.
Under a gauge change L shifts by q dχ/dt, a total time derivative, so the equations of motion are unchanged.
properties: L defined up to a total derivative

extra.description: Moves from the velocity description to the momentum description: p = ∂L/∂v, H = p·v − L.
The Hamiltonian state of a charge. Using kinetic momenta as coordinates instead puts the magnetic field into the symplectic form.
extra.math_structure: Cotangent bundle T*ℝ³ with symplectic form ω = dp∧dx.

extra.description: π = mv = p − qA. Gauge-invariant and measurable, for example from the curvature of a particle track. The canonical momentum p is not.
dF/dt = {F, H}. In a magnetic field the kinetic momenta do not commute: a classical non-commutativity that becomes Landau levels in quantum mechanics.
The field as a constrained Hamiltonian system. Gauss's law generates the gauge transformations.
extra.math_structure: Canonical pairs (A, Π = −ε₀E) with Gauss's law as a constraint, reduced by gauge orbits.

extra.description: Every continuous symmetry of the action yields a conservation law.
Total energy, momentum and angular momentum of matter plus field. Conservation holds only when the field's contributions are included.
Unifies grad, curl and div. d² = 0 contains both curl∘grad = 0 and div∘curl = 0.
α∧β = (−1)^{pq} β∧α: 1-forms anticommute, 2-forms commute. F∧F is a 4-form proportional to E·B.
Carries all metric (and constitutive) information. In form language it is the only place c and spacetime geometry enter Maxwell's equations.
The global geometric state. It can carry information, such as holonomy around holes, that no single local potential captures.
extra.math_structure: Principal U(1)-bundle over spacetime with a connection 1-form; potentials are its local expressions.

extra.description: In a non-abelian (Yang–Mills) theory the curvature is dA + A∧A. Electromagnetism's commutative group keeps it linear.
∮A·dl around a closed loop: gauge-invariant and equal to the enclosed flux. Around a solenoid it is non-zero on loops where B = 0. With ħ, the phase exp(iq∮A·dl/ħ) is the Aharonov–Bohm phase.
Energy density of cavity radiation per unit frequency at temperature T, measured with bolometers around 1900. It has a peak and falls at high frequency, which classical physics cannot reproduce.
Classical statistical mechanics gives every oscillator mean energy kT. Applied to infinitely many radiation modes, it gives infinite energy.
properties: ½kT per quadratic degree of freedom

extra.description: The first quantum rule. It ties a frequency, a wave property, to an energy, a particle property.
properties: links particle energy to wave frequency

extra.description: h ≈ 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, with ħ = h/2π. The quantum of action; classical physics is the regime where actions are large compared with ħ. Exact by definition in the 2019 SI.
Maximum kinetic energy of electrons ejected by light. It rises linearly with frequency above a threshold and does not depend on intensity.
A quantum of the electromagnetic field, with energy ħω and momentum ħk. Detected one at a time by photomultipliers and in Compton scattering.
Sharp wavelengths emitted or absorbed by atoms. Hydrogen's lines fit 1/λ = R(1/m² − 1/n²).
The old quantum theory's hybrid state: classical orbits with quantum selection rules. Superseded by quantum mechanics but historically the bridge.
extra.math_structure: Discrete set of classical orbits labelled by n, with angular momentum nħ.

extra.description: Shares every algebraic property of the Poisson bracket, which is why Dirac could map one to the other. Its non-zero value iħ is the quantum.
Observables become operators on states. Position and momentum no longer commute, so they cannot both be sharp: Heisenberg's uncertainty relation.
iħ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ. Linearity means quantum states superpose, the quantum descendant of the superposition principle of Part I.
Replaces the point in phase space. It assigns amplitudes, not definite values, to every observable.
extra.math_structure: Unit ray in a complex Hilbert space (a vector up to an overall phase).

extra.description: Connects the abstract state to what detectors record: frequencies of outcomes over many runs.
Probabilities and averages of measurement results over many identically prepared systems.
The quantum version of the classical kinetic momentum. It makes the potentials, not only the fields, act on charged quantum particles.
Discrete energies of a charge in a uniform magnetic field, seen in cyclotron resonance and the quantum Hall effect.
Shift of an interference pattern by qΦ_B/ħ for electrons passing around a region of magnetic flux they never enter.
The algebra needed to take a square root of p² − m²c². Its anticommutation, not commutation, is what produces spin ½.
The relativistic wave equation of the electron, the matter half of QED.
A spinor changes sign under a full 360° rotation, something no classical vector field does.
extra.math_structure: 4-component field transforming under SL(2,ℂ), the double cover of the Lorentz group.

extra.description: Ratio of the electron's magnetic moment to its spin in natural units. Dirac predicted exactly 2.
The electron's antiparticle, same mass, opposite charge. Electron–positron pairs are created and annihilated.
Quantizing each field mode as an oscillator. Commutators give bosons (photons); anticommutators give fermions (electrons).
properties: raise or lower quanta by one

extra.description: The state space of a quantum field, in which particle number can change.
extra.math_structure: Direct sum of n-particle Hilbert spaces, n = 0, 1, 2, …; basis labelled by occupation numbers.

extra.description: The quantized electromagnetic potential. Its expectation values in coherent states are classical fields.
extra.math_structure: Operator-valued distribution on Fock space (Coulomb gauge: transverse components only).

extra.description: Rate at which an excited atom emits a photon with no field present, set by vacuum fluctuations.
Attraction between uncharged parallel plates due to the change in zero-point energy of the field modes between them.
The electron as the quantum of a field. It annihilates electrons and creates positrons.
extra.math_structure: Anticommuting operator-valued spinor field on Fock space.

extra.description: α = e²/4πε₀ħc ≈ 1/137.036, the dimensionless strength of electromagnetism. Measured from the electron's g-factor and from atom-recoil experiments.
Expands amplitudes in powers of the small coupling α. Each higher order involves more virtual particles.
Splitting between hydrogen's 2S½ and 2P½ levels: about 1000 MHz in Lamb and Retherford's 1947 measurement, about 1058 MHz in later, more precise measurements.
a_e = (g − 2)/2 ≈ 0.00115965, measured by Kusch and Foley (1947) and today to about a tenth of a part per billion.
Expresses predictions in terms of measured quantities, so that infinities cancel. Later understood through the renormalization group.
properties: absorbs divergences into measured m and e

extra.description: Quantizes using the classical action directly, so the action principle of Part I becomes the core of quantum theory.
Pictorial rules for the terms of the perturbation series.
Packages everything that can be measured in a scattering experiment.
extra.math_structure: Unitary operator on Fock space mapping incoming to outgoing states.

extra.description: Scattering rates per unit flux, measured in collision experiments (Compton, Møller, Bhabha scattering).
The effective strength of electromagnetism at momentum transfer Q, measured at colliders: about 1/128 at the Z mass.
Demanding local phase invariance requires a connection, the electromagnetic potential, and fixes how it couples to charge.
The complete specification of quantum electrodynamics in one line: Dirac field plus Maxwell field, coupled through the covariant derivative.
Relations among amplitudes implied by gauge symmetry; they protect the theory's consistency through renormalization.

extra.title: Newton's second law
extra.formula: m dv/dt = F, dx/dt = v, integrated forward in time.

extra.title: Read off velocity
extra.formula: v = dx/dt.

extra.title: Position along a trajectory
extra.formula: The position component of the state of motion.

extra.title: Read positions off the configuration
extra.formula: A coordinate of the configuration is a position measurement.

extra.title: Coulomb force sum
extra.formula: Fᵢ = Σⱼ k qᵢqⱼ(xᵢ − xⱼ)/|xᵢ − xⱼ|³.

extra.title: Point charges as a density
extra.formula: ρ(x) = Σ qᵢ δ³(x − xᵢ).

extra.title: Total charge from density
extra.formula: Q = ∫ρ dV.

extra.title: Test-charge definition
extra.formula: E = lim F/q as q → 0.

extra.title: Evaluate the field at a point
extra.formula: The observable E(x₀) is the state E(·) evaluated at x₀.

extra.title: Gauss's law with symmetry
extra.formula: Avoids integration when symmetry fixes the field's shape.

extra.title: Static limit of the dynamical field
extra.formula: With ∂/∂t = 0 the electric part decouples and is curl-free.

extra.title: Direct flux integral
extra.formula: Φ_E = ∮E·dA.

extra.title: Gauss's law
extra.formula: Φ_E = Q_enc/ε₀.

extra.title: Potential from a line integral
extra.formula: φ(x) = −∫E·dl from an arbitrary reference point.

extra.title: Solve Poisson's equation
extra.formula: ∇²φ = −ρ/ε₀ with boundary conditions.

extra.title: Static limit of the gauge potential
extra.formula: For static fields in Coulomb gauge, the scalar part of the representative is the electrostatic potential.

extra.title: Energy as charge times potential
extra.formula: U = ½∫ρφ dV.

extra.title: Energy stored in the field
extra.formula: U = (ε₀/2)∫|E|² dV.

extra.title: Difference of potential values
extra.formula: ΔV = φ(b) − φ(a); the arbitrary constant cancels.

extra.title: Line integral of the field
extra.formula: ΔV = −∫ₐᵇ E·dl, path-independent in statics.

extra.title: Capacitance
extra.formula: C = Q/ΔV; linearity makes the ratio independent of Q.

extra.title: Current as flux of J
extra.formula: I = ∫J·dA.

extra.title: Resistance from voltage and current
extra.formula: R = ΔV/I.

extra.title: Local Ohm's law
extra.formula: J = σE inside a conductor.

extra.title: Density evolves by continuity
extra.formula: ∂ρ/∂t = −∇·J updates ρ in time.

extra.title: Biot–Savart integral
extra.formula: B(x) = (μ₀/4π)∫J × (x − x′)/|x − x′|³ d³x′.

extra.title: Ampère's law with symmetry
extra.formula: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enc.

extra.title: Evaluate the field at a point
extra.formula: B(x₀) from the field B(·).

extra.title: Infer B from the velocity-dependent force
extra.formula: Solve F − qE = q v×B for B using several velocities.

extra.title: Force on a current element
extra.formula: dF = I dl × B (Ampère, Laplace).

extra.title: Flux integral of B
extra.formula: Φ_B = ∫B·dA; any surface with the same boundary gives the same answer because ∇·B = 0.

extra.title: Flux from the loop integral of A
extra.formula: Φ_B = ∮A·dl by Stokes' theorem.

extra.title: Faraday's flux rule
extra.formula: ℰ = −dΦ_B/dt.

extra.title: Direct loop integral
extra.formula: ℰ = ∮(E + v×B)·dl.

extra.title: Measure the couplings
extra.formula: ε₀ from the strength of electric forces, μ₀ from forces between currents.

extra.title: Displacement current
extra.formula: Adding μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t to Ampère's law restores consistency with charge conservation.

extra.title: Maxwell's equations as forms
extra.formula: dF = 0 and d⋆F = μ₀⋆J.

extra.title: Predicted wave speed
extra.formula: Combining the curl equations gives wave equations with speed 1/√(μ₀ε₀).

extra.title: Fields from potentials
extra.formula: E = −∇φ − ∂A/∂t, B = ∇×A, the same for every member of the gauge class.

extra.title: Split F by an observer
extra.formula: E and B are the components of F relative to an observer's four-velocity.

extra.title: Energy density of the field
extra.formula: u = ½(ε₀|E|² + |B|²/μ₀).

extra.title: Force from the Maxwell stress
extra.formula: F = ∮σ·dA over a surface enclosing the charges (minus the change of field momentum inside, added after 1900).

extra.title: Retarded potentials
extra.formula: φ(x,t) = (1/4πε₀)∫ρ(x′, t − |x − x′|/c)/|x − x′| d³x′, and likewise for A.

extra.title: Gauge orbit of a pair
extra.formula: All pairs related by gauge transformations form one class.

extra.title: Existence of potentials
extra.formula: Fields obeying ∇·B = 0 and Faraday's law come from some (φ, A), at least locally.

extra.title: Pick a representative
extra.formula: A gauge condition selects a concrete A from the class.

extra.title: Poynting vector
extra.formula: S = E×B/μ₀.

extra.title: Mode expansion of free fields
extra.formula: Source-free solutions as sums of plane waves.

extra.title: Read off wave data
extra.formula: Each mode has definite k, ω = c|k| and polarization.

extra.title: Momentum density
extra.formula: g = S/c².

extra.title: Lorentz force law
extra.formula: F = q(E + v×B).

extra.title: Larmor formula
extra.formula: P = q²a²/(6πε₀c³) for slow charges.

extra.title: Flux of the Poynting vector
extra.formula: P = ∮S·dA over a large sphere.

extra.title: Assemble the four-potential
extra.formula: (φ/c, A) transform together as a four-vector.

extra.title: Assemble the four-current
extra.formula: J^μ = (cρ, J).

extra.title: Antisymmetrized derivative of A
extra.formula: F_μν = ∂_μA_ν − ∂_νA_μ (Minkowski).

extra.title: Contract the field tensor
extra.formula: F_μνF^μν ∝ |B|² − |E|²/c² and F_μνF̃^μν ∝ E·B.

extra.title: Stress–energy tensor
extra.formula: T^μν = (1/μ₀)(F^μα F^ν_α − ¼ g^μν F_αβ F^αβ).

extra.title: Euler–Lagrange equation for a charge
extra.formula: Gauge-dependent terms cancel and the result is q(E + v×B).

extra.title: Canonical momentum
extra.formula: p = ∂L/∂v = mv + qA.

extra.title: Subtract the potential
extra.formula: π = p − qA; the gauge shifts of p and qA cancel.

extra.title: Hamilton's equations
extra.formula: dx/dt = {x, H}, dp/dt = {p, H}.

extra.title: Hamiltonian field theory
extra.formula: Canonical pairs from the field Lagrangian, with Gauss's law as a constraint.

extra.title: Noether charges of matter plus field
extra.formula: Time translations give energy, space translations momentum, rotations angular momentum.

extra.title: Charge conservation from gauge symmetry
extra.formula: Invariance of the action under gauge changes forces ∂ρ/∂t + ∇·J = 0.

extra.title: F = dA
extra.formula: Gauge shifts A → A + dχ drop out since d²χ = 0.

extra.title: Invariants as forms
extra.formula: F∧F ∝ E·B and F∧⋆F ∝ |E|² − c²|B|².

extra.title: Conservation from d² = 0
extra.formula: d⋆J = μ₀⁻¹ d(d⋆F) = 0.

extra.title: Glue local potentials
extra.formula: Potentials on overlapping patches differ by gauge transformations, which glue them into a bundle.

extra.title: Curvature of the connection
extra.formula: F is the curvature 2-form of the U(1) connection.

extra.title: Parallel transport around a loop
extra.formula: Holonomy exp(i∮A); classically the loop integral ∮A·dl itself.

extra.title: Rayleigh–Jeans law (classical)
extra.formula: u(ν,T) = 8πν²kT/c³: correct at low frequency, infinite total energy.

extra.title: Planck's law
extra.formula: u(ν,T) = (8πhν³/c³)/(e^{hν/kT} − 1).

extra.title: Classical wave prediction
extra.formula: Electron energy should grow with intensity and arrive after a delay; neither is observed.

extra.title: Einstein's photoelectric equation
extra.formula: K_max = hν − W.

extra.title: Light quanta
extra.formula: E = hν, p = h/λ (Einstein 1905, Compton 1923).

extra.title: Classical atom (Larmor)
extra.formula: An orbiting electron radiates continuously and spirals into the nucleus within about 10⁻¹¹ s.

extra.title: Bohr's quantization
extra.formula: Angular momentum mvr = nħ selects the allowed orbits.

extra.title: Bohr's frequency rule
extra.formula: hν = Eₙ − Eₘ between stationary orbits.

extra.title: Phase-space functions become operators
extra.formula: f(x, p) → f(x̂, p̂), with an ordering choice.

extra.title: Canonical quantization of the state
extra.formula: Points (x, p) are replaced by wave functions ψ(x); x̂ multiplies, p̂ = −iħ ∂/∂x.

extra.title: Hydrogen from the Schrödinger equation
extra.formula: Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n² as eigenvalues of Ĥ.

extra.title: Born rule statistics
extra.formula: Prob(a) = |⟨a|ψ⟩|², ⟨Â⟩ = ⟨ψ|Â|ψ⟩.

extra.title: Quantize the kinetic momentum
extra.formula: π̂ = −iħ∇ − qA; a gauge change becomes a phase change of ψ.

extra.title: Landau quantization
extra.formula: Eₙ = ħω_c(n + ½), ω_c = qB/m.

extra.title: Aharonov–Bohm phase
extra.formula: Δθ = q∮A·dl/ħ = qΦ_B/ħ.

extra.title: Dirac's relativistic equation
extra.formula: (iħγ^μD_μ − mc)ψ = 0.

extra.title: Spinor solutions
extra.formula: Solutions carry spin ½ and come with positive and negative energy.

extra.title: Dirac's magnetic moment
extra.formula: g = 2 exactly at this level of the theory.

extra.title: Fine structure of hydrogen
extra.formula: Levels depend on n and total angular momentum j.

extra.title: Negative-energy solutions
extra.formula: Holes in the Dirac sea behave as antiparticles.

extra.title: Each mode is a quantum oscillator
extra.formula: a_k, a_k† with [a_k, a_k′†] = δ_kk′.

extra.title: Photons as field quanta
extra.formula: One photon = one excitation of a mode.

extra.title: Build Fock space
extra.formula: Apply creation operators to the vacuum |0⟩.

extra.title: Vacuum fluctuations drive emission
extra.formula: Dirac 1927: the rate scales as ω³ times the squared dipole matrix element.

extra.title: Canonical quantization of the field
extra.formula: [Âᵢ(x), Π̂ⱼ(y)] = iħ δ⊥ᵢⱼ(x − y) in Coulomb gauge.

extra.title: Coherent states (classical limit)
extra.formula: Glauber 1963: ⟨Ê⟩ and ⟨B̂⟩ obey Maxwell's equations; fluctuations are negligible for many photons.

extra.title: Zero-point energy between plates
extra.formula: F/A = −π²ħc/240d⁴.

extra.title: Quantize the Dirac field
extra.formula: Expand ψ in modes with anticommuting operators.

extra.title: Naive perturbation theory
extra.formula: Self-energy corrections come out infinite.

extra.title: Dirac's prediction
extra.formula: 2S½ and 2P½ exactly degenerate: no shift.

extra.title: Dirac's prediction
extra.formula: g = 2 exactly, so a = 0.

extra.title: Sum over histories
extra.formula: Amplitude = ∫Dx e^{iS[x]/ħ}.

extra.title: Stationary phase (classical limit)
extra.formula: When S ≫ ħ, only paths near δS = 0 survive.

extra.title: Expand the path integral
extra.formula: Each term of the series is a diagram.

extra.title: Sum diagrams into amplitudes
extra.formula: ⟨f|S|i⟩ = sum of diagrams.

extra.title: Cross sections from amplitudes
extra.formula: σ ∝ |⟨f|S|i⟩|² summed over final states.

extra.title: Schwinger's correction
extra.formula: a = α/2π + O(α²).

extra.title: Renormalized Lamb shift
extra.formula: Self-energy and vacuum polarization give about 1058 MHz.

extra.title: Vacuum polarization
extra.formula: Virtual pairs screen charge; α(Q) grows logarithmically with Q.

extra.title: Gauge the phase symmetry
extra.formula: Require invariance under ψ → e^{iqχ(x)/ħ}ψ.

extra.title: Assemble the QED Lagrangian
extra.formula: ℒ = ψ̄(iγ^μD_μ − m)ψ − ¼F_μνF^μν (natural units).

extra.title: Feynman rules from the Lagrangian
extra.formula: Propagators and vertices read off ℒ_QED.

extra.title: Gauge symmetry in amplitudes
extra.formula: k_μ M^μ = 0, Z₁ = Z₂.

extra.title: Modern QED prediction
extra.formula: a_e computed through order α⁵ (tenth-order diagrams), agreeing with measurement to about 10⁻¹² in g.
